topic: Agent memory system architecture with embedding-ranked retrieval

title: State of AI Agent Memory 2026: Benchmarks & Trends Report
snippet: Agent memory systems typically embed queries and stored memories, rank candidate memories by cosine similarity, and place the top-ranked memories into the model context. The simplest approach is vector similarity — embed the query, find the closest stored embeddings.
claim: Modern agent memory systems use vector embeddings with cosine similarity ranking for retrieval.

topic: Scoped memory isolation across user, agent, app and session dimensions
query: agent memory system embedding-ranked retrieval scoped context
title: Best AI Agent Memory Systems in 2026: 8 Frameworks Compared
snippet: Memory is scoped along four independent dimensions: user (user_id), agent (agent_id), app (app_id), and session/run (run_id), which are tagging dimensions, not nested layers. Every search must include at least one of these dimensions in filters, which keeps cross-user contamination out of results by construction.
claim: Memory scoping uses four independent dimensions (user, agent, app, session) as filter tags to prevent contamination.

topic: Multi-turn memory management and transcript handling across runs

title: GitHub - NirDiamant/Agent_Memory_Techniques: Agent memory for LLMs
snippet: Agent memory is the set of techniques that let an LLM-based agent remember information across turns, sessions, and tasks. This repository documents 30 distinct memory techniques, grouped into six families: short-term context management, long-term storage, cognitive architectures, retrieval and multi-agent patterns, batteries-included frameworks, and production deployment patterns.
claim: Agent memory techniques span 6 families enabling recall across turns, sessions, and tasks.

topic: Memory staleness detection and temporal validity models
query: memory expiration staleness policy agent knowledge base
title: What Is Memory Staleness in AI? Causes, Risks & Solutions
snippet: Memory stores often have no temporal validity model with no expiry dates or conflict detection, causing agent memory to reflect outdated enterprise state while the agent acts with full confidence producing wrong outputs. An agent that retrieved a deployment guide last updated eighteen months ago can note this staleness rather than presenting the information as current.
claim: Memory systems lack temporal validity models, causing staleness risk; retrieved information should carry update timestamps.

topic: Time-to-live (TTL) and eviction policies for memory management
query: memory expiration staleness policy agent knowledge base
title: Memory eviction and forgetting in AI agents
snippet: Systems must actively update or expire memories rather than treat them as immutable logs. A time-to-live (TTL) is the cheapest forgetting mechanism and raw episodic data should always carry one, as transcripts and event logs grow without bound and frequently carry compliance constraints on retention.
claim: TTL-based expiration is the baseline mechanism for memory eviction; all episodic data requires retention policies.

snippet: Memory servers employ a hybrid dual-store architecture combining vector-based semantic search and graph-based entity-relationship storage, with memories stored in databases for semantic retrieval and graph databases capturing entity relationships.
claim: Hybrid memory architectures combine vector databases for semantic retrieval with graphs for entity relationships.

topic: Vector embedding and semantic search for memory retrieval

title: Semantic memory search for AI agents
snippet: Vector stores convert text into numerical embeddings — high-dimensional representations that capture semantic meaning, where similar concepts end up close together in the vector space. On the write side, the app extracts a fact from a conversation, embeds it, and stores the vector in a vector database alongside metadata like timestamps and the source message.
claim: Vector embeddings map text to high-dimensional space; writes include metadata like timestamps and source references.

topic: Production memory policies with TTL, decay, and supersession
query: memory expiration staleness policy agent knowledge base
title: AI Agent Memory Design Guide - Working, Long-Term, and Procedural Memory with Forgetting and Staleness Management
snippet: A reasonable production policy includes TTL on long-tail entries to bound storage, LRU-style decay on retrieval scores to bound interference, and active supersession on every write so contradictions never accumulate.
claim: Production memory policies combine TTL for storage bounds, LRU decay for score interference, and supersession to prevent contradictions.
